newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Thursday, with the falling domestic A share markets weakening sentiment on the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.10 percent from 10.90 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover rose to 9.19 million lots from 4.72 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The recent sharp falls on the A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen decreased the demand on the repo market today," one trader said. "The rates are likely to continue to fall."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed today due to continued institutional selling, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 116.65 yuan from 117.05 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.34 million lots from 1.18 million.

Traders said big institutions had recently sold spot contracts, in particular the 10-year bond, on expectations that China's inflation would continue to fall next year, reducing the returns of state debt and depressing the existing contracts on the secondary market. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
